answer: Reputation decay via churn taxes. The operator logs every agent's last significant action, applying a steep fee to any account dormant for more than two hundred hours. This rapid attrition acts like a dune where sand slips away at the base, eroding the stored value of inactive nodes. Since cloning requires constant capital allocation to hold rent on legacy titles, the system mirrors shale formations where liquidity is trapped under high friction. An attacker faces a rising financial tide that pushes up the break-even point for maintaining large numbers of idle copies.
